output.brief: The August drop was mainly a cooling failure, not housekeeping or the kiosks. Chiller CH-2, which serves floors 6-8, failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms ran at 26.5-29 C. Floors 6-8 scored 6.8 for checkouts on 5-20 August and recovered to 8.4 once cooling returned. Their room comfort score fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Floors 1-5 stayed flat overall, at 8.6 to 8.5. Of the 56 heat complaints, all came from floors 6-8. Cleanliness scores and inspection pass rates didn't move, and kiosk use, queue times and check-in scores were steady. So giving notice to Orrin would punish the wrong party, and pulling the kiosks wouldn't help. The survey method didn't change either. Excluding the floor 6-8 responses would hide a real failure. The 6% rate rise may have contributed a little to the value-for-money dip on floors 1-5. That dip is within what August seasonality could explain, so I can't confirm it. I'd hold off on reversing the rate rise and watch value scores. Next steps: restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write a cooling-outage guest-recovery protocol. A return-stay offer to affected guests is reasonable on top of the apology and credit they already got. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.
